long_biography.plain_text:
Trained as a civil engineer in Madrid, Florentino Pérez began in private business before holding several public-administration posts. He returned to commerce in 1983 as chief executive and a leading shareholder of Construcciones Padrós, then combined construction businesses to create the platform that became ACS in 1997. He has remained the infrastructure group's executive chairman while retaining a substantial personal shareholding.

Pérez's other defining institution is Real Madrid. During his first period as club president, he pursued star signings, stronger commercial operations and major facilities investment. He later resigned, returned after a three-year absence and oversaw another sustained period of sporting success and redevelopment of the Santiago Bernabéu. The football club is member-owned, making his presidency a governance role rather than a personal ownership interest.
